subject: Embeddings model fit validation — follow-up & benchmark links
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Embeddings model fit validation — follow-up & next steps

Hi Emily — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

Goal: validate / select an embeddings model for Voxly's semantic search for FAQ and knowledge-base content. Primary constraints you mentioned: 1) high semantic recall for short queries (user question → passage), 2) < 1s lookup latency for production, 3) index size limits for your current cloud provider, and 4) sensitivity to embedding dimensionality for downstream ranking models.

What we propose next:
- Run a 5k-sample validation across your historical queries and KB passages using two candidate models: redwood-embed-compact-v1 (512d) and redwood-embed-extended-v2 (1536d).
- Metrics: MRR, MAP@10, Recall@100, cosine-similarity distribution (to check collapse/drift), and ANN latency at 1k/10k/100k index sizes.
- Deliverables: benchmark CSV, recommended model + quantization profile, prompt sets used for synthetic queries, and a short migration plan for index configuration.

Attachments: semantic_search_benchmarks.csv (sample results), prompt_sets_v1.md (query categories & templates). Drive folder with full artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-voxly-benchmarks

Proposed timing: we can kick off the run by Mon 11/30 and share initial results by Thu 12/3. Can you confirm:
- Access: a read-only dump of the KB + a sampling of anonymized queries (S3 link or shared Drive).
- Priority metric: is MRR at top-1 or Recall@10 more important for your team?

Recommended short note on expected tradeoffs: 512d (compact) will be cheaper and smaller index footprint — often fine where latency and cost dominate. 1536d tends to give nicer separability (higher MRR) on nuanced semantic differences but increases index storage and ANN latency; we can mitigate with quantization and shard routing.

Next step: If you sign off on the sample size & candidate models above, I’ll assign Marissa to run the validation on Redwood Dedicated and Neha will review for drift/regression checks.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Thanks Marcus — that all sounds good. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we sign off: 
1) Dimensionality: our current ranking stack expects 768 or fewer dims to avoid re-training downstream models (we know this is a constraint). If the 1536d model is materially better, would you recommend projecting or fine-tuning to 768?
2) Indexing: we're using Pinecone in us-west and need to keep storage under ~250GB for the current budget. Do you have ballpark index-size estimates for 5M passages at 512d vs 1536d (with typical compressed quantization)?
3) Latency: is the <1s end-to-end target including ANN lookup + re-ranking? We can stretch to 1.5s if needed.

Also looping in Samir (cc) from our infra team for any S3 access questions. Happy to approve the sample run once we have the dimension guidance and a rough cost/size estimate.

Emily — thanks for the questions, good ones. Short answers + plan: 

1) Dimensionality tradeoff: given your downstream constraint (<=768), our recommendation is to try the 512d compact model first (redwood-embed-compact-v1). In our benchmarks for KB-style semantic search, 512d hit recall@10 within ~3-5% of 1536d on many enterprise KBs while saving ~60% on index size. If 512d misses a critical slice (we'll detect via per-query-group MRR), we can try a projection path: 1536d -> 768d using PCA or an autoencoder in a small retraining step, but that adds complexity.

2) Index size estimates (very approximate, post-quantization):
- 5M passages @ 512d -> ~40–60GB (with 8-bit PQ/OPQ style quantization)
- 5M passages @ 1536d -> ~120–180GB (same quant profile)
These are ballpark; we’ll produce exact numbers after the run with real distributions.

3) Latency: when we say <1s, that's ANN lookup + single-pass nearest-neighbor scoring. Re-ranking (dense-sparse hybrid or cross-encoder) is additional — for production we typically do ANN fetch + fast re-ranker (token-light model) to stay under 1.5s. If you need strict <1s including rerank, we can tune sharding and prefetching, but expect higher infra costs.

Plan: we’ll start with redwood-embed-compact-v1 (512d) and redwood-embed-extended-v2 (1536d) for comparison as planned. Marissa will run the 5k sampling and return the CSV with the metric breakdown. Neha will run the drift/regression checks and signal any quality regressions vs your historical baseline.

I’ll schedule a 30-min sync for Thu 12/3 to walk through the results — does 11:00am PT work?

Thanks —
Marcus
